title: 1. Hook: The Mystery of the Missing Spider
text: Imagine you walk into a garden and notice all the spiders have magically disappeared. At first, you might be happy. But a few days later, you see something strange. The plants are covered in holes, and there are flies everywhere! Why did this happen?

title: 2. Socratic Thinking
text: What do you think happens to the frogs if there are no more insects left to eat? And what happens to the snakes that eat the frogs? Think carefully.

content.title: 3. Discovery: The Invisible Strings
content.description: Just like a spider builds a web, nature has invisible strings connecting everything. If one string breaks, the whole web shakes!

title: 4. Reveal: The Web of Life
text: In nature, plants, animals, birds, insects, and humans all depend on each other to survive. We also depend on non-living things like the Sun, Air, Water, and Soil. This beautiful connection is called the Web of Life.

content.definition: The way living things rely on each other and their environment to survive.
Everything around us, including living things like plants and animals, and non-living things like air, water, and sunlight.

content.question: What would happen to a plant if there was no sunlight or water?
options: It would dry up and die.

content.question: Which of these is a non-living thing that we need to survive?

title: 6. Reflection
text: Close your eyes and think about your day. Write down three things from nature you used today. (Hint: What did you drink? What did you breathe?)

title: 7. Connection
text: Think about how this connects to what we learned about plants! Plants make food using sunlight, water, and air. Animals eat plants. We eat plants and some animals. We are all connected in this big beautiful Web of Life.

content.title: Careful!
content.text: Many students think humans only need food from shops. Remember, even the food in the shop originally comes from plants and animals in nature!

content.title: 8. Mastery: Draw Your Own Web
content.text: Draw yourself in the middle of a blank page. Now draw all the things you need to live (Sun, Water, Plants, Animals). Draw lines connecting you to them. You just drew your own Web of Life!

content.title: Teacher's Note
content.text: Encourage students to understand that they are a part of nature, not separate from it. Humans are an integral part of the Web of Life.
